summary.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail market share 29% vs 31% a year earlier; new-to-insurance mix in fresh retail 94% vs 90%. Proprietary channels (agency and D2C) are 90%+ of retail business.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

guidance_outlook: Insurance revenue growth is expected to rise from 13.4% towards 15-16% as the quarters progress, and to increase further in FY28.
Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.
Steady-state ROE target is mid-to-high teens on an Ind AS basis; no specific number given.
Fresh-business growth expected to moderate in H2 FY27 and into H1 FY28 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds; management agreed this framing.
capex_capacity: Agency network added about 20,000 agents in the quarter to 8.5 lakh; agent productivity up 19% YoY.
Non-metro fresh business growth is 3.5x metro growth.
Customer app has about 16 million downloads and 1.5 million+ monthly active users.
97% of new applications are digitally sourced; generative AI being layered on existing AI/ML claims analytics.
Long-term policies are about 40% of retail fresh business; fresh-to-renewal share about 20:80 in insurance revenue.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.question: How will GWP growth of 19% convert into insurance revenue growth, and when will they converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

risks_watch: Seasonal Q2 loss ratio pressure from vector-borne and infectious diseases.
Regulatory changes to commissions and claims reforms; management declined to comment until rules are final.
Retail market share fell to 29% from 31%; clean like-for-like comparison not expected until FY28.
Fresh growth may moderate in H2 FY27 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds.
Other expenses rose about 23% YoY to Rs 283 crore, driven by loss of GST input credit and annual rate hikes.
Accounting questions open: finance income under PAA on long-term contracts (Rs 38.8 crore) and DAC balance were not fully explained.
summary.management_tone: Confident on underwriting trajectory and ROE glide path, but guarded on specifics: no loss ratio guidance, no telemedicine claim numbers, and no commentary on pending regulation. Some answers were deferred to offline discussion (DAC, finance income treatment).

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 16 crore in Q1 FY26

key_quotes: We believe that consistency is important and we'll focus on profitable growth.
This marks the fourth successive quarter of improvement in core underwriting profitability, underscoring the consistency of performance.
We are not giving any guidance for loss ratio improvement.
We don't want to give any number in particular, but that is the glide path that we are going towards.
We don't want to divert from that and chase growth for the sake of it.

adds.what: Agency network added about 20,000 agents in the quarter to 8.5 lakh (headcount addition, not plant or fleet capacity)

growth.why: Management guides insurance revenue growth rising from 13.4% in Q1 toward 15-16% through the year and further in FY28, but fresh-business growth is expected to moderate in H2 FY27, and no company-owned capacity or capex was discussed.
